rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for steady progress or the course of something, including the passage of time.

example.english: This project's march toward completion is going more smoothly than expected.
example.traditional: 呢個計劃嘅進程比預期順利。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 gai3 waak6 ge3 zeon3 cing4 bei2 jyu6 kei4 seon6 lei6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for soldiers or military units marching on foot.

example.english: They march to the parade ground every morning.
example.traditional: 佢哋每日朝早行軍去操場。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 mui5 jat6 ziu1 zou2 haang4 gwan1 heoi3 cou1 coeng4

rows.note: Use this for a military march or the movement of soldiers in formation.

example.english: The troops march toward the summit.
example.jyutping: bou6 deoi6 hoeng3 zyu6 saan1 deng2 haang4 gwan1

rows.note: Use this specifically for marching drill by soldiers, bands, or participants in a ceremony.

example.english: The students in the band march in drill following commands.
example.traditional: 學生樂隊跟住口令做步操。
example.jyutping: hok6 saang1 ngok6 deoi6 gan1 zyu6 hau2 ling6 zou6 bou6 cou1

rows.note: Use this everyday pattern when someone leads or takes another person somewhere on foot.

example.english: I march my son to the park every Sunday.
example.traditional: 我每個星期日帶阿仔去公園。
example.jyutping: ngo5 mui5 go3 sing1 kei4 jat6 daai3 aa3 zai2 heoi3 gung1 jyun4

rows.note: Use this when someone is forcibly escorted or taken under guard, especially a prisoner.

example.english: The police march the suspect to court.
example.jyutping: ging2 caat3 aat3 go3 ji4 faan6 heoi3 faat3 ting4

rows.note: Use this formal phrase when a person, project, or situation is making steady progress.

example.english: This project continues to march steadily forward.
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 hong6 muk6 wan2 bou6 cin4 zeon3
